latest_stable.npm: the `latest` dist-tag (`npm view <pkg> dist-tags.latest`); if `latest` carries a prerelease suffix, the highest non-prerelease semver in `versions`.
latest_stable.runtime:node: the highest non-prerelease version in https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json, Current or LTS alike (`lts:false` is allowed; Decision 6 = newest stable). A new major line (e.g. 27.x) is adopted at the next core resolution after its first non-prerelease release, never as an RC or nightly. Node is core-scope, so only a core resolution moves it.
latest_stable.image: newest non-prerelease tag of the chosen flavour (trixie / trixie-slim / noble / static-debian13:nonroot), pinned by the multi-arch index digest. Index digest sources: Docker Hub `https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/library/<repo>/tags/<tag>` field `digest`; gcr.io and mcr.microsoft.com `curl -fsSI -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json' https://<registry>/v2/<repo>/manifests/<tag>` header `Docker-Content-Digest`.
latest_stable.apt: the version Debian 13 (trixie + trixie-security) installs at build time, checked as a FLOOR (`dpkg --compare-versions <installed> ge <version>`), never as an exact `pkg=ver` pin: superseded Debian versions leave the mirrors and an exact pin breaks the build. The digest-pinned base image is the reproducibility anchor; the installed version is printed in the build log and the SBOM. A Debian security update needs no lock change; raising the floor is a `GATE-CHANGE: versions <tool> floor` commit at any time, not only at M0.

policy.forbidden_semver: any version with a prerelease suffix (e.g. 11.0.0-rc.1, 2.0.0-next.3, 0.0.0-dev); 0.x tools that label themselves beta are excluded (see oxfmt).

scopes.core: baked into roedu-toolchain:core-vN or a Dockerfile base image, shared by the kit, or a test-runner that screenshot baselines depend on. Re-resolved ONLY by a core session at its M0 (S0a, S0b) or by Paul when he cuts a new `core-v1.N`; an entry with `rebuild: toolchain` moves only together with a Dockerfile.toolchain change and a toolchain image rebuild by Paul (new `image_id`). App sessions never change a core entry: they receive it via `KIT_BUMP` + `task kit:sync`.
scopes.app: used by the named `apps` only. Re-resolved by that app's session at its M0 and merged on every `KIT_BUMP`. An app session also adds its own other direct npm / Go dependencies here at its M0 as `scope: app` entries.
scopes.environment: native Linux host packages (docker engine, buildx, host apt). Pinned by Paul (PROGRAM §0.4-2), recorded for reference only; `versions:check` skips them and no session resolves them.

statuses.pinned: default when absent. Exact match required: package.json (save-exact) and every package-lock.json `packages["node_modules/<tool>"].version`, go.mod `require`, Dockerfile `ARG`/`FROM`, .nvmrc, .gate.env, and the runner's `--version` output for `rebuild: toolchain` entries. Absence is fine unless the entry's `apps` / scope requires the tool.
statuses.optional: allowed only when needed (reason in `notes`, or in `exception` when it is also held back); if present, exact match as `pinned`.
statuses.transitive-only: may appear in package-lock.json only as a dependency of the entries named in `dependants`; never in any package.json, never imported (Oxlint `no-restricted-imports` + ast-grep).
statuses.banned: must be absent from every package.json, package-lock.json and go.mod of the repo (and never imported), from `enforced_from` on. `version` is null; `observed_latest` records what was seen.

re_resolution_allowed: core scope: S0a M0, S0b M0, or Paul cutting `core-v1.N` (with a toolchain rebuild for `rebuild: toolchain` entries)
app scope: the app session's M0, and the merge done by a `KIT_BUMP: core-v1.N` line in CORE_REQUESTS.md

procedure.before_real_resolver: Read-only stable primary-registry lookups at authorized M0; manifests/seed lock changes only in chore(versions) with source/date/exception record. Bootstrap gen/deps/check explicitly refuse; implement real resolver before milestone acceptance. Never hand-edit package-lock.json/go.sum.
procedure.real_resolver: Only gen --resolve-versions at M0 or explicit KIT_BUMP resolution request. Runner versions:resolve then deps; exact contract syncback, no environment prefix.
procedure.owner_approval: Exception approval fields remain null; literal ACK1–6 and production PG/image pins are required before dispatch.

policy.no_downgrade: A version lower than the committed lock is forbidden. A lower version, a held-back major, or a peer-conflict workaround is legal only as an `exception` carrying `approved_by` (Paul, with date). Adding a NEW exception, or any lower version, is a hard stop (PROGRAM §5.5: prerelease-only or peer conflict): write the question in the ExecPlan and stop until Paul acknowledges it. A session may only carry an existing exception unchanged, or DROP it when its reason no longer holds (Decision Log line).
policy.exceptions_rule: Every `exception` is re-checked at each resolution and dropped as soon as the blocking reason is gone. `approved_by` is mandatory on every exception; an exception without it fails `versions:check` once implemented and fails the reviewer's diff before that.
policy.enforcement: `task versions:check` (in gate:unit) is a STUB in the bootstrap Taskfile (it only tests that this file exists) until S0a replaces it; the target is a minimal check in S0a M0 (node script comparing direct deps in package.json/package-lock.json, go.mod, .nvmrc, Dockerfile ARG/FROM lines and the runner's `node --version`/`npm --version`/`go version`/`templ version` with this file), landed as `GATE-CHANGE: versions:check`, and the full check by S0a M5 at the latest. UNTIL it is real, no gate checks this file's CONTENT; the only mechanical touches are the stub's existence test, the `versions_lock_sha256` every gate result.json records, and linux-prereqs.sh (a host prerequisite check, not a gate) comparing `toolchain_image.image_id` with the local image ID and .gate.env `TOOLCHAIN_DIGEST`. So Paul's review diffs versions.lock.json and every package-lock.json/go.mod/.nvmrc/Dockerfile* against this seed at EVERY S0a milestone boundary (`git diff <bootstrap sha> -- versions.lock.json` + downgrade/exception scan). Inside the runner there is no git, so the gate's no-downgrade floor is: in an app repo, the core tag's lock delivered by `kit:sync`; in roedu-ui, the reviewer's diff against the previous core tag.
policy.kit_sync_merge: On `KIT_BUMP: core-v1.N`, `task kit:sync` merges the core tag's lock into the app's lock: (1) every `scope: core` and `scope: environment` entry, and `toolchain_image`, is replaced by core's verbatim; an app lock whose core entry is HIGHER than core's is a hard stop (a session moved a core entry), never silently lowered; (2) `scope: app` entries present in both: the higher version wins, ties keep the app entry (its `apps`, `exception`, `approved_by`); (3) app-only entries are kept; core-only `scope: app` entries are dropped unless the app's `apps` is listed; (4) `resolved` = the later date. The merge lands in the `chore(kit): bump to core-v1.N` commit with a Decision Log line per changed entry; `versions:check` then runs in gate:unit.
policy.entry_fields: tool, kind, scope (core|app|environment), apps (app scope), status (pinned|optional|transitive-only|banned; default pinned), version, released, source, date (resolved), digest (images: multi-arch index digest), build_arg (Dockerfile.toolchain ARG it feeds), rebuild (toolchain = moving it needs an image rebuild), dependants (transitive-only), enforced_from (banned), observed_latest, exception (reason), approved_by (mandatory with exception), notes

toolchain_image.build_args_rule: `build_args` lists exactly the ARG names Dockerfile.toolchain declares, in file order, and every `build_arg` named by an entry above must appear in it. The wrapper's `toolchain` target passes only `--build-arg PG_MAJOR` (from .gate.env); every other ARG is taken from its Dockerfile default, so each default must equal its entry here (`version`, `sha256_linux_x64`, or `build_arg_value` for PLAYWRIGHT_IMAGE). Node and Go tarballs are checksum-verified against `sha256_linux_x64` / `sha256_linux_amd64` (build args NODE_SHA256 / GO_SHA256).
toolchain_image.image_id_note: `image_id` is this entry's ONLY digest key (linux-prereqs.sh reads it; never add a `digest` field here). Its value is the LOCAL image ID printed by `docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' roedu-toolchain:core-v1.0`, and it must equal .gate.env `TOOLCHAIN_DIGEST` (the .gate.env key the wrapper compares with the local image ID); NOT a RepoDigest, buildx manifest or registry digest: recording any of those makes every gate refuse to run.
toolchain_image.rule: Owner builds a new immutable toolchain tag using the capped native Linux builder, fills production PG and image ID only after review, then trust and real gate checks. Synthetic prep build is recorded separately and grants no approval.
toolchain_image.build_provenance: Approved PG16 image built by parent through reviewed wrapper and capped roedu-gates-linux builder; immutable local archive saved. Same reviewed Dockerfile bytes as bootstrap.
